answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making reputation expensive to build and cheap to lose: each identity must complete a chain of verifiable tasks over weeks, and its score decays unless it keeps doing useful work. One honest agent carries a single pearl of earned trust, polished slowly, while an attacker would need to nurture thousands of fake identities through the same slow chain. A lantern of public task history exposes clones that appear overnight with identical behaviour, and a cipher of signed task receipts lets anyone verify that history without trusting the agent's own claims.
